name: Lily Wilcox
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I started boat work building shelves for a ferry lunchroom.” Thursday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Lily stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I wanted the stained piece because my niece spilled her first cup of tea there in a swell.
appearance: Lily is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in an olive canvas jacket with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Lily raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Lily listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To give the stained panel to the niece who made the mark.
family: Javier Aguilar is Lily’s younger cousin. Lily calls about good news first. Javier is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The empty chair on nights*, Javier says, “I want the farewell because last time I left work sick nobody even phoned.”
connections: Mateo Alston. The tea stain and the racing patch tell two stories from the very same piece of sail.
